title: Purpose: Con Miras A, Con Vistas A and Con el Fin de

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *con el fin de* from B1 Unit 32 and the phrases of purpose *con miras a* and *con vistas a* ("with a view to") from B2 Unit 12. They name what you do something for, with an infinitive or a noun. The candombe tradition is full of that kind of thinking: people prepare and protect with a goal in mind.

sections.title: Purpose phrases
rows: Las comparsas ensayan con miras a las Llamadas de febrero.
*con miras a* + noun: with a view to
Los tamborileros ensayan con vistas a desfilar en febrero.
*con vistas a* + infinitive: with a view to doing
La UNESCO incluyó el candombe con el fin de ayudar a protegerlo.
*con el fin de* + infinitive: in order to
Con miras al desfile, las comparsas afinan los tambores.

items.spanish: Las comparsas ensayan con miras a las Llamadas de febrero.
items.english: The comparsas rehearse with the February Llamadas in view.

items.spanish: Los tamborileros ensayan con vistas a desfilar en febrero.
items.english: The drummers rehearse with a view to marching in February.

items.spanish: La UNESCO incluyó el candombe con el fin de ayudar a protegerlo.
items.english: UNESCO listed candombe in order to help protect it.

items.spanish: Con miras al desfile, las comparsas afinan los tambores.
items.english: With the parade in view, the comparsas tune the drums.

sections.content: The preposition is always *a* after *miras* and *vistas*, and always *de* after *con el fin*: never *con el fin por* or *con miras en*. After *con el fin de* use an infinitive when the subject is the same. These phrases sound planned and a little formal; for simple purposes *para* is still the natural word.
